claim: Distance ease values between real 3D-scanned straight-fit dresses and virtual dresses simulated in Lectra Modaris 3D differed by up to 29.9% (1.16 cm) at the bust girth and varied from 7.3% (0.51 cm) to 47.3% (4.30 cm) at the waist due to wrinkling.
stance_target: discrepancies and technical limitations in 3D CAD virtual fit simulation of ease allowance at bust and waist zones
scope_conditions: Straight-fit woven dresses (5 fabrics, KES-F tested) on VITUS Smart XXL 3D scanned mannequins vs Lectra Modaris 3D
quoted_support: Distance ease of virtual and scanned garments was compared in bust and waist cross-sections. It was defined that distance ease values at bust girth of real and virtual dresses differed till 29.9 % (1.16 cm), while at waist varied from 7.3 % (0.51 cm) to 47.3 % (4.30 cm) because of wrinkles in this area.

claim: As mannequin size increases, the visual appearance and shape fluency similarity between 3D virtual garments and real physical garments decreases.
stance_target: degradation of 3D CAD virtual fit accuracy across larger graded sizes
scope_conditions: Women's mannequins of different sizes scanned with VITUS Smart XXL vs Modaris 3D simulation
quoted_support: Generally, appearance of the virtual dresses was similar to real dresses with some differences in garment shape fluency, however by increasing of the mannequin size, similarities decreased.

claim: 3D CAD garment simulation systems fail to accurately reflect woven fabrics with very high shear rigidity (G), only achieving reliable virtual try-on accuracy when fabric shear rigidity is below 1.6 N/m·° and warp tensile strain is above 1.80%.
stance_target: mechanical fabric property thresholds where 3D CAD simulation diverges from real physical garment fit
scope_conditions: Woven fabrics tested with KES-F and simulated in Lectra Modaris 3D
quoted_support: It was assumed that very high shear rigidity G could not be very well reflected in 3D CAD system, therefore differences between virtual and real dresses appearance occurred. So, comparative study showed that the accuracy of virtual try-on was quite useful comparing to real garments, if shear rigidity of fabrics was lower than 1.6 N/m*º and tensile strain in warp direction was higher than 1.80 %.
